display_title: Targeted Delivery of Exosome-Derived miRNA-185-5p Inhibitor via Liposomes Alleviates Apoptosis and Cuproptosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy
summary: A preclinical study evaluated peptide-functionalized miR-185-5p-inhibitor liposomes in DOX-injured cells and mice, with formulation, biodistribution, cardiac phenotyping and cell-death-associated readouts. No human therapeutic efficacy was established.
research_question: In the tested doxorubicin-associated cardiac injury models, does delivery of a miR-185-5p inhibitor in peptide-functionalized liposomes alter cardiac function, injury and cell-death-associated readouts?
author_summary: This preclinical investigation assessed miR-185-5p-inhibitor-loaded liposomes in doxorubicin (DOX)-injured H9C2 cells, human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes in vitro and male C57BL/6 mouse models. The delivery vehicle is a peptide-functionalized liposome, not a clinical infusion of patient-derived exosomes. Loaded particles had a reported DLS diameter of 172.35 ± 0.8 nm and encapsulation efficiency of 98.0 ± 1.2%; TEM and DLS size measurements represent different measurement contexts. Mouse experiments reported greater cardiac fluorescence with the targeting peptide and improvements in echocardiographic and histological readouts. Cell experiments assessed apoptosis- and cuproptosis-associated proteins and other injury signals. These findings support the tested preclinical delivery strategy; they do not establish human efficacy, human safety, a general DCM therapy or complete pathway-specific causality. Abstract-only survival/percentage claims and unresolved protocol-reporting details are not promoted into independently verified quantitative key findings.

what_this_adds: A peptide-functionalized liposomal delivery approach for a miR-185-5p inhibitory payload.
Preclinical biodistribution and cardiac-function/histology evaluation in DOX-associated injury models.
Cell-injury-associated molecular readouts and limited experimental tolerability assessment, with explicit separation from human treatment evidence.

supports: Formulation characterization and labeled-preparation biodistribution in the tested experiments.
Improvement in reported cardiac function and histology in the DOX-associated mouse model.
Changes in cell-death-associated readouts in H9C2 and iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte experiments.
Limited tolerability observations within the tested settings.
does_not_establish: Human treatment efficacy, clinical safety or approval of the liposomal miR-185-5p intervention.
A universally effective therapy for all etiologies of dilated cardiomyopathy.
Exosome infusion or clinical transplantation of patient-derived vesicles.
Exclusive cardiac targeting or an intact-drug tissue dose inferred solely from fluorescence.
Complete miRNA-target/pathway-specific causality from marker changes alone.
An independently verified quantitative survival advantage or harmonized percentage-effect estimate from the abstract alone.

limitations: The experimental disease model is DOX-associated injury; generalization to other causes of human DCM is unestablished.
The main text and abstract differ in quantitative presentation; abstract-only survival language and percentage effects are not elevated to independently verified key findings.
The printed animal-model dosing description requires source/author clarification before experimental reproduction; no corrected dose or protocol recommendation is supplied.
Human iPSC-derived cells, cultured-cell replicates and assay-specific mouse n values are not interchangeable biological units.
Fluorescence targeting, marker changes and limited organ testing do not establish clinical biodistribution, complete causal mechanism or human safety.

qa.question: Is this a human DCM treatment trial?
qa.answer: No. It uses DOX-injured cell systems and mouse models. Human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes remain an in-vitro system, not treated patients.

qa.question: What is being delivered: exosomes or liposomes?
qa.answer: The experimental carrier is a peptide-functionalized liposome carrying a miR-185-5p inhibitory payload. The exosome-related title and earlier expression work should not be read as a clinical exosome infusion.

qa.question: How were the particles characterized?
qa.answer: The loaded formulation had a DLS diameter of 172.35 ± 0.8 nm, encapsulation efficiency of 98.0 ± 1.2% and approximately 80% release at 48 hours. TEM describes approximately 100-nm morphology; that is not the same measurement as hydrodynamic size.

qa.question: What evidence supports cardiac targeting?
qa.answer: The targeting-peptide preparation showed greater cardiac fluorescence than the non-targeted preparation in the reported mouse comparison. Fluorescence does not by itself quantify an intact active-drug dose or establish exclusive heart delivery.

qa.question: What cardiac and cellular outcomes were reported?
qa.answer: Mouse echocardiography and histology showed favorable changes under the tested conditions, and cell experiments showed changes in apoptosis- and cuproptosis-associated proteins. These are preclinical readouts, not human outcomes.

qa.question: Does the article establish safety or a survival benefit in people?
qa.answer: No. Its tolerability testing is limited and experimental. Abstract-only survival and percentage claims are not treated here as independently verified key outcomes, and no human treatment cohort is present.

related_papers.relationship: Earlier human DCM-HF plasma exosomal miRNA profiling, cited as reference 10 by the liposomal study. Its miR-185-5p evidence is discovery-stage association/network prioritization, not an externally qRT-PCR-validated causal finding or a human intervention.

Related preclinical cardio-oncology intervention research on NLRP3/ICI cardiac injury. The injury agents, interventions and mechanistic questions differ; the studies are not direct replication of one treatment effect.

provenance.review_basis: Published main text, tables and figure legends at the cited primary sources. No independent reanalysis of participant-level data; unresolved reporting differences are identified in the evidence scope.
provenance.data_availability: The article states that datasets are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request. No public dataset accession or code repository was verified. Selected quantitative claims are anchored to main-text/figure descriptions; a complete raw-data or supplementary-protocol audit was not performed.
